items.title: Jerusalem's holy sites empty as Iran war upends Easter, Passover

featured_image.name: Jerusalem heads into a subdued Passover, Easter under the shadow war

items.description:
Jerusalem's Old City, normally teeming with pilgrims during the overlapping spring holidays, has fallen near-silent this year as the Iran-Israel war enters its sixth week, upending Easter and Passover observances in one of the world's holiest places.

Since the start of the U.S.-Israel military operation against Iran on February 28, Israeli authorities have barred access to the Old City for anyone other than residents and shop owners, according to the Times of Israel. Shops along the ancient stone streets sit shuttered under Home Front Command directives, and holy sites including the Western Wall, Al-Aqsa Mosque, and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre have been closed to the general public since March 6. Nationwide, gatherings remain limited to 100 people indoors and 50 outdoors, provided a bomb shelter can be reached within 90 seconds.[1][2][3]

items.title: Strikes on Iran's Mahshahr petrochemical zone kill 5, wound 170

featured_image.name: US and Israel strike petrochemical facilities in southwest Iran

items.description: US and Israeli airstrikes struck the Mahshahr Special Petrochemical Economic Zone in southwestern Iran on Saturday, killing at least five people and wounding 170 others in an attack targeting one of the country's most important industrial hubs. The Israel Defense Forces confirmed responsibility for the strikes, saying the complex housed "one of the primary locations where a critical component for ballistic missiles is produced."[1][2]

items.title: Artemis II crew fixes frozen toilet line on way to Moon

featured_image.name: NASA Answers Your Most Pressing Artemis II Questions

items.description: Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft are now more than halfway to the Moon on a historic mission, though an intermittent toilet malfunction has added an unscripted challenge to humanity's first lunar voyage in more than half a century.

items.title: Nine-spin quantum system outperforms classical AI in weather forecasting

featured_image.name: Using Quantum Computing to Tell the Weather

items.description:
A quantum processor made from just nine atomic spins has beaten classical neural networks containing thousands of nodes at predicting real-world weather patterns, in what researchers describe as the first experimental demonstration of a quantum machine learning system outperforming large-scale classical models on a practical task.

The study, published in Physical Review Letters on Friday, was led by scientists at the University of Science and Technology of China in Hefei, with collaborators at Fudan University, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Zhejiang University.[1][2][3]

items.title: Hezbollah launches 60 attacks as Israeli strikes kill civilians in Lebanon

featured_image.name: Israeli attacks on southern Lebanon kill two girls, damage hospital

items.description: Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah intensified on Saturday as the Lebanese militant group struck an Israeli Merkava tank with a guided missile in southern Lebanon, setting it ablaze, while Israeli airstrikes killed at least two girls and wounded 40 people across the country's south, according to Lebanon's health ministry.[1][2]

items.title: Iran rejects Pakistan-led ceasefire talks with U.S., threatens second shipping chokepoint

featured_image.name: Iran's parliament speaker hints at targeting Bab el-Mandeb Strait

items.description: Diplomatic efforts to halt the widening conflict between the United States and Iran collapsed on Friday after Tehran formally rejected a Pakistan-brokered mediation initiative, refusing to send officials to Islamabad and dismissing Washington's demands as "unacceptable," according to The Wall Street Journal. The breakdown leaves no clear path to a ceasefire as violence in the region intensifies and global shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains paralyzed.[1]

items.title: Israeli airstrike kills one in Gaza as ceasefire violations mount

featured_image.name: Israeli air strikes on Gaza kill four Palestinians - Al Jazeera

items.description:
Israeli forces struck a civilian vehicle at the entrance of the al-Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza on Saturday evening, killing one Palestinian man and injuring several others who were transported to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah, according to the Palestinian news agency WAFA. The Middle East Monitor reported three others were wounded in the attack on Salah al-Din Street.[1][2]

The strike came on what Palestinian authorities count as the 177th day since the ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas took effect in October 2025. Despite the deal, Israeli forces have continued near-daily airstrikes, drone attacks, artillery shelling, and naval fire across the Strip.

items.title: Archbishop Mullally to call for Middle East peace in first Easter sermon

featured_image.name: Archbishop to pray for Middle East peace in first Easter sermon

items.description: The Archbishop of Canterbury, Dame Sarah Mullally, is set to use her first Easter sermon to pray for "an end to the violence and destruction" in the Middle East, as the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran enters its sixth week and religious leaders around the world intensify calls for peace during the holiest weekend on the Christian calendar.[1][2]

items.title: U.N. to vote on Hormuz resolution after France, Russia, China strip military language

featured_image.name: Bahrain waters down UN proposal over opposition to allowing force ...

items.description:
French President Emmanuel Macron warned Thursday that the ongoing U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran cannot resolve Tehran's nuclear ambitions, calling instead for a diplomatic and regulatory framework that would include inspections and strict limits on uranium enrichment.

"A selective military action, even for a few weeks, will not resolve the nuclear issue in the long term," Macron said upon arriving in Seoul for a state visit to South Korea, according to AFP. "What is needed is the strictest possible framework to prevent further enrichment."[1][2]

Macron cautioned that without sustained diplomacy, the current crisis could repeat itself. "If there is no framework for diplomatic and technical negotiations, the situation can deteriorate again in a few months or a few years," he said.[3][1]

items.title: Iran launches drone strikes on US bases in UAE, Kuwait

featured_image.name: Iran Army conducts drone strikes against US bases in UAE, Kuwait

items.description: Iran's military carried out a fresh wave of drone attacks against American military installations in the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait on Saturday, as the US-Israeli war against Iran entered its sixth week.

items.title: Russia escalates aerial assaults as Ukraine's Patriot missile stocks run critically low

featured_image.name: U.S. sending dozens of Patriot missiles from Israel to Ukraine

items.description: As the United States pours interceptor missiles into its campaign against Iran in the Persian Gulf, Russia has seized the moment to launch an unrelenting aerial assault on Ukraine, deliberately targeting the country's dwindling supply of Patriot air defense missiles with wave after wave of drones and ballistic strikes.

items.title: Brent crude hits $141 as Hormuz closure fuels worst energy crisis since 1970s

featured_image.name: Brent oil price for actual cargo soars to $141, highest ...

items.description:
More than five weeks after the United States and Israel launched Operation Epic Fury against Iran, the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz has plunged global energy markets into their worst crisis since the 1970s, with Brent crude surging past $112 per barrel and governments worldwide scrambling to shield their economies from deepening fuel shortages.

The war began on February 28, 2026, when U.S. and Israeli forces conducted nearly 900 strikes in 12 hours targeting Iranian military infrastructure and leadership, killing Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. Iran retaliated with missile and drone attacks across the Middle East, including strikes on oil infrastructure and vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, through which roughly 20% of the world's oil supply normally passes. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps formally declared the strait closed to vessels traveling to or from the U.S., Israel, and their allies on March 27.[1][2]

items.title: Philippines declares energy emergency as oil crisis grips Southeast Asia

featured_image.name: Philippines says it is working with Washington to obtain oil ...

items.description: The escalating Middle East conflict has thrown Southeast Asia's energy security into sharp relief, with analysts and policymakers pressing ASEAN member states to mount a coordinated regional response before fragmented national measures deepen the economic damage. As oil and gas flows through the Strait of Hormuz remain disrupted, the bloc faces what researchers describe as a more complex supply shock than any in recent memory — one that could persist well beyond a ceasefire.

items.title: Pope Leo urges world not to 'grow numb' to war at Easter vigil

featured_image.name: VATICAN-RELIGION-EASTER-VIGIL

items.description: Pope Leo XIV celebrated his first Easter Vigil as pontiff on Saturday night at St. Peter's Basilica, calling on the world's 1.4 billion Catholics not to become paralyzed by the scale of global conflicts but to work toward peace and harmony.

items.title: Tehran rejects Trump's 48-hour ultimatum on Strait of Hormuz

featured_image.name: All hell will reign down': Trump gives Iran 48-hour ultimatum over Strait  of Hormuz

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps launched a fresh wave of missile and drone strikes targeting facilities in the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, and Israel on Thursday, framing the assault as direct retaliation for US-Israeli airstrikes that shut down the country's two largest steel plants. The escalation marked the 90th phase of what Tehran calls "Operation True Promise IV" and came as the broader US-Israel war against Iran entered its fifth week with no diplomatic resolution in sight.

items.title: Israel strikes over 200 targets across Iran, Lebanon

featured_image.name: IDF carries out over 70 strikes across Iran targeting ballistic missile ...

items.description: The Israeli Defense Forces carried out one of its most expansive operations of the ongoing war over the weekend, striking more than 200 military positions across Iran and Lebanon as fighting on multiple fronts showed no signs of abating.

items.title: Trump claims Iran military leaders 'terminated' in Tehran strike

featured_image.name: Trump: U.S. will bomb Iran "back to stone ages" over next 2-3 weeks

items.description:
President Trump escalated his rhetoric against Iran on Saturday, warning that Tehran has 48 hours to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or reach a peace deal before the United States unleashes "all hell" on the country. The ultimatum, posted on Truth Social, sets a deadline of Monday, April 6, as the war enters its sixth week with no end in sight.[1][2][3]

"Remember when I gave Iran ten days to MAKE A DEAL or OPEN UP THE HORMUZ STRAIT," Trump wrote. "Time is running out — 48 hours before all Hell will reign down on them. Glory be to GOD!" It marks the second time Trump has issued such a deadline; a similar 48-hour ultimatum on March 21 was eventually postponed after what Trump described as "good and productive" peace talks — claims Iranian state media denied.[4][5][6][1]

items.title: Iran threatens 'crushing' strikes on US, Israeli assets across Middle East

featured_image.name: Iran vows response to US strikes as it hits back at Israel

items.description: Iran's armed forces on Saturday issued their most sweeping threat yet in the five-week-old war, warning that any further US strikes on Iranian infrastructure would be met with "sustained and destructive" attacks on all American and Israeli assets across the Middle East. The escalation came as Tehran rejected a US-backed 48-hour ceasefire proposal, leaving diplomatic efforts in disarray.

items.title: US-Israeli jets strike Tehran's Shahid Beheshti University

featured_image.name: US-Israeli Airstrikes Target Shahid Beheshti University in ...

items.description: American and Israeli fighter jets struck Shahid Beheshti University in Tehran on Friday, destroying a research facility and a women's dormitory at one of Iran's leading academic institutions, according to Iranian state media. The attack marks the latest escalation in a campaign that has now damaged universities, hospitals, and research centers across the country, drawing a sharp rebuke from more than 100 international law experts who warn the strikes may constitute war crimes.

items.title: Iran cluster bombs wound 6 in central Israel as war enters sixth week

featured_image.name: Video shows damage to Tel Aviv buildings after Iranian missile attack

items.description: Iran fired several salvos of ballistic missiles at Israel on Saturday, causing extensive damage to homes across the Tel Aviv metropolitan area and wounding six people, as the war that began February 28 entered its sixth week with no signs of easing across the broader Middle East.
